question.text: How many postal ballots will Correos report as admitted for Spain's 29 November 2026 general election in the most recent figure it publishes on or before 26 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the cumulative national number of postal ballots reported by Correos as admitted, deposited or sent ("votos admitidos", "votos emitidos", "votos depositados" or "enviados") for the 29 November 2026 Spanish general election, in the most recent Correos press release with a publication date of 26 November 2026 or earlier (Correos dates its releases in Madrid local time), as listed in its press room at https://www.correos.com/press-release-category/voto-por-correo/ . Counts of postal-vote applications ("solicitudes") are not used. Only the headline national cumulative total stated by Correos is used, exactly as published; no adjustment is made and regional or foreign-constituency (CERA) breakdowns are not summed. As an example of the metric, Correos' 22 July 2023 release (https://www.correos.com/sala-prensa/exito-en-la-gestion-del-voto-por-correo-que-marca-record-historico-con-2-471-935-votos-admitidos-para-las-elecciones-generales) reported 2,471,935 ballots admitted for the 23 July 2023 election, which would resolve as 2471935; if Correos states such a total only approximately (e.g. "more than 2.4 million"), the stated number is used (2,400,000). If no cumulative ballots-admitted figure for the 29N election has been published by that cutoff, the question is annulled.
question.fine_print: If Correos' press-room listing is unavailable or not yet updated, the figure published in the corresponding Correos press note (including its PDF version) or reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) citing Correos is used. Any extension of the ballot-deposit deadline by the Junta Electoral Central does not change the cutoff date.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: I read the Correos "Voto por correo" press-room listing directly. The newest entry is "El próximo jueves, 19 de noviembre, finaliza el plazo para solicitar el voto por correo" (Madrid, 16 Nov 2026). It covers procedure only and gives no count of applications or ballots. The entry before it, dated 10 Nov ("Así es el voto por correo en las Elecciones Generales del 29 de noviembre"), sets out the calendar and also has no figures. [Correos](https://www.correos.com/press-release-category/voto-por-correo/)
- There is no data file or API behind the listing. Figures only ever appear in the text of press releases.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. So far Correos has published no cumulative figure for 29N, neither applications nor ballots.
- 2026-11-16: Herqles reports that neither Interior nor Correos has released any aggregate count of applications or ballots for 29N. This differs from July 2023, when Correos figures were public about 40 days out (around 600,000 applications in the first days, more than 2.3 million by mid-July). Interior receives daily data from Correos under Orden PJC/1461/2025 but says it uses it only to check that the service is working. [Herqles](https://herqles.com/2026/11/16/interior-voto-correo-29n-datos/)
- The usual Correos practice of publishing applications figures during the campaign has not happened this time. That is a small warning sign for annulment, although Correos did publish both applications and ballot figures for the Andalusian election in May 2026.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Several outlets repeat the deadlines: applications close 19 Nov, ballots must be deposited by 25 Nov, ballot papers have been sent out since 9 Nov, and Correos has 2,303 offices. [Antena 3](https://www.antena3.com/noticias/espana/estos-son-ultimos-dias-pedir-voto-correo-29n-asi-funciona-estos-son-plazos_202611166afaaa0403bbf30bb04d9488.html); [elEconomista](https://www.eleconomista.es/actualidad/noticias/14028185/11/26/fechas-clave-para-el-voto-por-correo-esta-semana-acaba-el-plazo-maximo-para-solicitarlo-pero-se-puede-enviar-hasta-antes-del-25-de-noviembre.html)
- 2026-11-15: Telecinco reports that ballot and envelope distribution continues until 22 Nov. [Telecinco](https://www.telecinco.es/noticias/espana/20261115/elecciones-generales-2026-plazos-solicitud-voto-correo-ultimo-dia-entregar_18_020667405.html)
- 2026-11-03: PP and Vox asked the Junta Electoral Central (JEC) to have Correos' daily data shared with the JEC and all parties. Vox also wants it published on the Correos website. I found no final JEC ruling. [El Español](https://www.elespanol.com/espana/politica/20261103/vox-pide-junta-electoral-obligue-gobierno-compartir-participacion-diaria-voto-correo-forma-inmediata/1003744443764_0.html); [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2026/11/03/el-pp-pide-a-la-junta-electoral-acceder-a-la-informacion-de-correos-del-voto-por-correo/)
- Background, already in the question: Abascal has urged voters not to vote by post, and the government calls the system "100% secure".

## 4. Base rates
National general elections (ballots admitted, per Correos):
- April 2019: 1,241,716. [Correos 2023](https://www.correos.com/sala-prensa/exito-en-la-gestion-del-voto-por-correo-que-marca-record-historico-con-2-471-935-votos-admitidos-para-las-elecciones-generales)
- November 2019: 918,455 applications as of 31 Oct 2019, before the last day was counted, about 30% below April. [El Independiente](https://www.elindependiente.com/politica/2019/10/31/correo-tramita-30-menos-peticiones-voto-28-a/) Correos reported 900,188 ballots sent on the deposit-deadline day (8 Nov, a deadline the JEC had extended). A later reference gives 924,403 postal voters.
- July 2023: 2,622,808 applications, 2,461,284 ballots on the night of 20-21 Jul, final 2,471,935 on 22 Jul (94.2%).
- Applicants who end up not voting: 6-9%, so ballots are usually 91-94% of applications.

Regional elections in the 2025-26 cycle, as a guide to the current climate:
- Andalusia, 17 May 2026: 178,541 applications, up 1.11% on 2022. Correos reported 163,510 ballots admitted (91.58%) on 14 May, one day after the 13 May deposit deadline. [Andalucía Informa](https://andaluciainforma.es/?p=29737); [El Debate](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/andalucia/20260511/voto-postal-alcanza-maximos-historicos-andalucia-pese-apagon-correos_416198.html)
- Aragón, 8 Feb 2026: 21,467 postal votes, down 37.2% on May 2023 (figure from the Aragón government). [El Debate](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/20260208/voto-correo-desploma-aragon-cae-372-cns_383129.html)

Timing: the release this question needs has usually come out 0-2 days after the deposit deadline. The examples are 8 Nov 2019 (deadline day), 20-22 Jul 2023, and 14 May 2026 (the day after the deadline). A release on 26 Nov would therefore be typical and falls inside the cutoff.

Seasonality: November general elections drew about 0.9 million ballots (2019), compared with 2.47 million for a summer election (2023). The only November data point is 2019, which was also a repeat election with voter fatigue. Without an applications count I cannot tell whether 2026 is running above or below past years.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on postal-ballot counts.
- Related markets: Polymarket gives PP 80.5% to win and PP+Vox a majority at 87%. Kalshi gives Feijóo 84% to be PM and Vox's median at about 19%. These show a highly salient election, but Vox voters may be steering away from postal voting.

## 6. Upcoming events
- 19 Nov: application deadline. The JEC could extend it, as it did in Andalusia in 2026.
- About 20-23 Nov: a likely Correos release with total applications admitted. This would be the strongest anchor, since ballots have run at roughly 91-94% of applications.
- Any JEC ruling on the PP/Vox request for the daily data.
- 25 Nov: deposit deadline. A JEC extension would not move the 26 Nov cutoff.
- 25-26 Nov: the most likely window for the release with ballots admitted. If Correos waits until 27 Nov or later, the question would be annulled or would resolve on an earlier, partial figure.
- Weather: not relevant.

Note: an Ávila item claiming 8,945 applications in "August 2026" for the general election looks like a misdated archive page, so I have ignored it. [Ávilared](https://avilared.com/art/70806/correos-ha-admitido-cerca-de-9000-solicitudes-de-voto-por-correo-en-avila)

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: I read the Correos press-room listing directly. The newest release is "El próximo jueves, 19 de noviembre, finaliza el plazo para solicitar el voto por correo" (Madrid, 16 Nov 2026). It has no figures, only deadlines: applications close 19 Nov, ballots must be deposited by 25 Nov, and the census office has been mailing ballot packs since 9 Nov. [Correos](https://www.correos.com/press-release-category/voto-por-correo/)
- 2026-11-10: "Así es el voto por correo en las Elecciones Generales del 29 de noviembre" covers procedure only. It notes that voters can, for the first time in a general election, get an email confirming their vote reached the polling table, and that ballot transport now uses GPS beacons and 24/7 video surveillance. [Correos](https://www.correos.com/press-release-category/voto-por-correo/)
- Neither release has any count of applications or ballots for 29N. There is no data file behind the page. I found no higher-frequency public series (for example daily counts).

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The application total should come out after 19 Nov, and the ballots figure around 25-26 Nov.
- On timing, Correos has usually published the ballots figure the day after the deposit deadline. Here that would be 26 Nov, the last day inside the cutoff:
  - July 2023: deadline 20 July, 2,461,284 published 21 July, final 2,471,935 on 22 July.
  - Andalusia 2026: deadline 13 May, figure reported 14 May.
  - November 2019: published on the deadline day itself (8 Nov), 900,188.
- If Correos publishes nothing by 26 Nov, the question is annulled. If its last release before the cutoff is an earlier partial count, that partial count is what resolves.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Several outlets repeat the deadlines (applications by 19 Nov, deposit by 25 Nov) and say Correos has 2,303 offices. None gives an application count. [elEconomista](https://www.eleconomista.es/actualidad/noticias/14028185/11/26/fechas-clave-para-el-voto-por-correo-esta-semana-acaba-el-plazo-maximo-para-solicitarlo-pero-se-puede-enviar-hasta-antes-del-25-de-noviembre.html); [Antena 3](https://www.antena3.com/noticias/espana/estos-son-ultimos-dias-pedir-voto-correo-29n-asi-funciona-estos-son-plazos_202611166afaaa0403bbf30bb04d9488.html)

- 2026-11-14: Correos' director of operations defended the system's safeguards after fraud claims (as summarised by the news API). [Diario Vasco](https://www.diariovasco.com/politica/proceso-seguro-garantias-funciona-voto-correo-espana-20261009000341-ntrc.html)
- 2026-10-06: Esdiario says it was too early to know application numbers. It argues 29N will look more like November 2019 than July 2023, pointing to postal-service costs of about €56.5M in November 2019 versus €101.5M in July 2023. [Esdiario](https://www.esdiario.com/nacional/261006/199537/carambola-millonaria-29n-esconde-detras-voto-correo_amp.html)
- Around 2026-10-05: Abascal and Ayuso questioned postal voting, and Abascal urged people to vote in person. I could not confirm the exact date. [Diario de León](https://www.diariodeleon.es/nacional/261005/2099374/abascal-ayuso-cuestionan-voto-correo-podra-solicitar-manana-29n.html); [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/politica/abascal-se-niega-a-respaldar-la-limpieza-del-voto-por-correo-al-no-poder-garantizar-su-proteccion/)
- 2026-06-23: Congress rejected Vox's bill to reform postal voting. [El Independiente](https://www.elindependiente.com/espana/2026/06/23/vox-reforma-voto-correo-fraudes-congreso-sanchez/)

## 4. Base rates
Correos figures for past general elections:
- **April 2019:** 1,241,716 ballots admitted; about 1.3M applications. [Correos 2023](https://www.correos.com/sala-prensa/exito-en-la-gestion-del-voto-por-correo-que-marca-record-historico-con-2-471-935-votos-admitidos-para-las-elecciones-generales)
- **November 2019:**
  - Applications were just under 1M, about 30% below April 2019 (Vozpópuli cited 918k before the last day's applications were counted). [El Independiente](https://www.elindependiente.com/politica/2019/10/31/correo-tramita-30-menos-peticiones-voto-28-a/)
  - Correos reported 900,188 sent on 8 Nov 2019. [Correos](https://www.correos.com/sala-prensa/900-000-ciudadanos-ya-han-enviado-su-voto-por-correo-para-las-elecciones-a-cortes-generales-del-10-de-noviembre)
  - A later figure of 924,403 is cited by Cronista, quoting Correos. [Cronista](https://www.cronista.com/espana/actualidad-es/elecciones-generales-el-voto-por-correo-alcanzo-la-cifra-mas-alta-registrada-en-la-historia-de-la-democracia-espanola)
- **July 2023:** 2,622,808 applications, then 2,461,284 ballots (21 July) and 2,471,935 final (22 July). That is 94.2% of applications.

How many applicants actually vote:
- Historically 91-94%.
- In the most recent election, Andalusia in May 2026, 163,510 ballots came from 178,541 applications (91.58%). Applications were about 1.1% above 2022 and ballots about the same as 2022, so the Vox campaign did not visibly cut postal voting there. [Andalucía Informa](https://andaluciainforma.es/?p=29737); [El Debate](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/andalucia/20260511/voto-postal-alcanza-maximos-historicos-andalucia-pese-apagon-correos_416198.html)

Season: the only comparable November general election is 2019, with roughly 0.90-0.92M ballots. Summer elections drew about 2.5 times as many. 2019 was also the fourth general election in four years, and voter fatigue cut postal voting then.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market or expert forecast on the number of postal ballots.
- Related markets on 2026-11-16:
  - Polymarket gives PP 80.5% to win and PP+Vox a majority 87%.
  - Kalshi puts Feijóo at 84% to be the next PM, and Vox reaching 65+ seats at 55%.
- None of these bears directly on the postal-ballot count.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 19 Nov: application deadline. The Junta Electoral Central could extend it, as it did in Andalusia 2026 and in 2023.
- Shortly after 19 Nov: Correos release with the total applications admitted. This will be the main anchor, since 91-94% of applicants usually vote.
- 22 Nov: last ballot packs mailed. 21-26 Nov: deposit window for voters abroad (CERA) at consulates.
- 25 Nov: deposit deadline. A JEC extension would not move the 26 Nov cutoff.
- 26 Nov: the likely date of the ballots-admitted release. A release dated 27 Nov or later would not count.
- Weather is not relevant, apart from possible local disruption.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain. The resolving figure should appear between 25 and 26 November 2026, and the cutoff is 26 November in Madrid time.

(b) The latest known value from Correos, as of 16 November 2026, is nothing. Correos has published no cumulative applications or ballots figure for 29N. Its 10 November and 16 November releases cover procedure only.

(c) If nothing changed, no ballots figure would be published and the question would be annulled. For the distribution I condition on a figure being published. History suggests a release 0 to 2 days after the 25 November deadline.

(d) If the current trend continued, the outcome would be roughly 1.0 to 1.4 million. The reasoning:
- Non-summer general elections have drawn about 0.9 to 1.3 million ballots: 1.24 million in April 2019 and about 0.92 million in November 2019.
- Postal voting has become more familiar since 2023.
- Andalusia in May 2026 was flat to slightly up on 2022.
- Against that, Vox discourages postal voting, and Aragón's postal vote fell sharply.
- Ballots usually run at 91 to 94% of applications.

(e) Historical variation: between general elections the totals range from 0.9 to 2.5 million, a swing of more than 2.5 times. Seasonality and salience drive most of that. A release on deadline day or the night after usually captures 97 to 99% of the final total. An earlier partial release could capture much less.

(f) No markets or experts forecast this figure. Election markets show a highly salient contest, with PP favoured and PP plus Vox likely to win a majority. High salience could raise turnout, possibly including PSOE-leaning postal voters.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: Correos, under political pressure, publishes only a mid-period partial figure, such as "500,000 have already sent their vote" around 22 to 24 November, and nothing more by the 26 November cutoff. Vox's boycott also suppresses postal demand.
- High: polarisation and travel around the long weekend push applications toward 2 million or more, as in summer 2023, with a full count published on 26 November.
